newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook-Mogas bearish, fuel oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook-Mogas bearish, fuel oil firm.

text.p: Asian refiners are under pressure to cut gasoline production this week after prices slumped to a six-month low amid two-year high stocks, industry sources said on Monday.
"The market is so flushed with oil, there is a need to cut output," a refiner in Singapore said.
Meanwhile, fuel oil was expected to be supported on strong buying support. Jet and gas oil were expected to be supported, both by a trader's buying.
Gasoline prices in Singapore plunged to their lowest level in six months. The 95-octane unleaded grade was offered at $24.00 per barrel, fob, on Thursday, the lowest since early October.
Prices have slipped from just above $29.00 since early March as stocks in Singapore have reached critical levels with supplies flooding in from the Middle East, Thailand and South Korea.

Light distillates stocks, which have been rising steadily since the week ending March 12, rose to a two-year high of 7.603 million barrels for the week ending April 16, Trade Development Board figures showed.
Although light distillates stocks comprise gasoline, reformate and naphtha, traders said the barrels were mostly gasoline.
Refiners in Singapore said lower petrol prices were squeezing profits from reforming, the secondary refining process that converts naphtha into reformate, a gasoline blending component.
The gasoline yield is currently just around $3.00 to $3.50 per barrel more than naphtha, the feedstock used in its production.
This is far below the breakeven cost of production, which is around $4.00-$4.50. The profit margin in producing gasoline from naphtha in early March was around $5.40 per barrel, traders said.

Little support was expected from the West. The American Petroleum Institute last Wednesday forecast gasoline supply in the U.S. would be more than adequate to meet peak summer demand, even on the most bullish demand forecasts.
"We haven't found the bottom yet.. we have been offering and offering but nobody wants to take us out," a seller said on the Singapore market.
Regional demand was mute with the exception of Taiwan's 95-octane reformate buying tender for May/June. It closes April 21 and is valid for two days.

Naphtha prices also fell to record-seven month low in Singapore amid poor fundamental support. Weak demand for prompt cargoes depressed premiums for Singapore barrels to just 50 cents per barrel over spot quotes and wiped out the backwardation to place May swaps on par with June.

In comparison, Asian fuel oil is the bull of the barrel and prices are poised to soar on projections of lower exports from South Korea and Kuwait, as well as strong demand from China, the region's main importer.
Kuwait is expected to half exports to two cargoes starting in May, while South Korean monthly exports of 600,000 tonnes would also be cut by nearly a quarter amid refinery turnarounds.

Traders said domestic demand was rising in Kuwaiti to meet summer air-conditioning and maintenance work at Kuwait's biggest refinery, the 420,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Mina Al-Ahmadi until end-April would further cut exports.
Traders said while poor bunker fuel demand in Fujairah has prompted two oil trading companies to move more than 80,000 tonnes to Singapore, the excess cargoes would be easily absorb.

"Yes, the market in the near term or the next two to three weeks may still be depressed but prices should rise in the second half of May when Asia's refinery shutdown season begins," a trader with a European firm said.
Meanwhile, Chinese demand was expected to be strong in May, at more than 500,000 tonnes and slightly higher than April.

Demand from Taiwan and India would also support prices, traders said. Taiwan's tender to buy more than 400,000 tonnes of fuel between June and November closes April 23 while India's to buy 30,000-tonnes for May 6-10 delivery closes April 24.
The Singapore trader who has bought about 14 million barrels of gas oil since early March, switched to supporting jet fuel, buying 600,000 barrels last week.
But traders said the jet fuel market was in contango. Regional demand for prompt cargoes was soft while they expect demand to pick up in later months.
